{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>CONFIDENTIALITY/NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1>September 12, 2007</SPAN 1>
<SPAN 2>Vector Capital Corporation</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>456 Montgomery Street, 19th Floor</SPAN 3>
<SPAN 4>San Francisco, CA 94104</SPAN 4>
<SPAN 5>Ladies and Gentlemen:</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>In connection with the expression of interest by Vector Capital Corporation (“Vector”) in a transaction with Captaris, Inc. (“Captaris”), Captaris will make available to Vector certain confidential and proprietary information concerning its business, financial condition, operations, assets and liabilities. </SPAN 6><SPAN 7>As a condition to such information being made available to Vector and Vector’s potential financing sources and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, agents or advisors (including, without limitation, attorneys, accountants, consultants, bankers and financial advisors) (collectively, “Representatives”), Vector agrees to treat any information concerning Captaris (whether prepared by Captaris, its advisors or otherwise and irrespective of the form of communication) which is furnished pursuant to this letter agreement to Vector or to its Representatives now or in the future by or on behalf of Captaris (such information herein collectively referred to as the “Evaluation Material”) in accordance with the provisions of this letter agreement, and to take or abstain from taking certain other actions hereinafter set forth. </SPAN 7><SPAN 8>The term “person” as used in this letter agreement shall be broadly interpreted to including the media and any corporation, partnership, group, individual or other entity.</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>The term “Evaluation Material” also shall be deemed to include all notes, analyses, compilations, studies, interpretations or other documents prepared by Vector or its Representatives to the extent they contain, reflect or are based upon, in whole or in part, the information furnished to Vector or its Representatives pursuant hereto. </SPAN 9><SPAN 10>The term “Evaluation Material” does not include information which </SPAN 10><SPAN 11>(i) is or becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of a disclosure by Vector or its Representatives in contravention of this agreement, </SPAN 11><SPAN 12>(ii) was within Vector’s possession prior to its being furnished to Vector by or on behalf of Captaris pursuant hereto, provided that the source of such information was not known by Vector to be bound by a confidentiality agreement with or other contractual, legal or fiduciary obligation of confidentiality to Captaris or any other party with respect to such information; </SPAN 12><SPAN 13>(iii) becomes available to Vector on a nonconfidential basis from a source other than Captaris or any of its Representatives, provided that such source was not known by Vector to be bound by a confidentiality agreement with or other contractual, legal or fiduciary obligation of confidentiality to Captaris or any other party with respect to such information; or </SPAN 13><SPAN 14>(iv) is independently developed by Vector without the use of any Evaluation Material and without any other violation of this agreement.</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>Vector hereby agrees that it and its </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>Representatives shall use the Evaluation Material solely for the purpose of evaluating a possible transaction between the parties, that the</SPAN 16>
<SPAN 17>Evaluation Material will be kept confidential and that Vector and its Representatives will not disclose any of the Evaluation Material in any manner whatsoever; provided, however, that </SPAN 17><SPAN 18>(i) Vector may make any disclosure of such information to which Captaris gives its prior written consent and </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>(ii) any of such information may be disclosed by Vector to its Representatives who need to know such information for the sole purpose of evaluating and implementing a possible transaction between the parties, who shall keep such information confidential and who are provided with a copy of this letter agreement. </SPAN 19><SPAN 20>In any event, Vector shall be responsible for any breach of this letter agreement by any of its Representatives, and Vector agrees, at its sole expense, to take reasonable measures (including but not limited to court proceedings) to restrain its Representatives from disclosure or use of the Evaluation Material in contravention of this agreement.</SPAN 20>
<SPAN 21>In addition, except as required by law or any rule of any self-regulatory organization, each of Captaris and Vector agrees that, without the prior written consent of the other party, it and its Representatives will not disclose to any other person the fact that the Evaluation Material has been exchanged, that discussions or negotiations are or may be taking place concerning a possible transaction involving the parties or any of the terms, conditions or other facts with respect thereto (including the status thereof) unless such first party has determined in good faith, after consultation with outside counsel, that such disclosure is required in order to avoid a violation of law or any rule of any self-regulatory organization.</SPAN 21>
<SPAN 22>In the event that </SPAN 22><SPAN 23>(i) Vector or any of its Representatives are requested or required (by oral questions, interrogatories, requests for information or documents in legal proceedings, subpoena, civil investigative demand or other similar process or law or any rule of any self-regulatory organization) to disclose any of the Evaluation Material furnished by Captaris or </SPAN 23><SPAN 24>(ii) Vector or any of its Representative or Captaris or any of its Representatives are requested or required (by oral questions, interrogatories, requests for information or documents in legal proceedings, subpoena, civil investigative demand or other similar process or law or any rule of any self-regulatory organization) to disclose any of the information described in the preceding paragraph (the “Other Confidential Information”)), then Vector or Captaris, as applicable (the “Disclosure Party”) shall, to the extent permitted by applicable law, provide Captaris or Vector, as applicable (the “Other Party”) with prompt written notice of any such request or requirement so that the Other Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy and/or waive compliance with the provisions of this letter agreement. </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>If, in the absence of any protective order or other remedy or the receipt of a waiver by the Other Party, the Disclosure Party or any of its Representatives determines in good faith, after consultation with the Disclosure Party’s outside counsel or such Representative’s counsel, as applicable, that it is legally compelled to disclose Evaluation Material (or any of the Other Confidential Information), the Disclosure Party or its Representative may, without liability hereunder, disclose only that portion of the Evaluation Material or Other Confidential Information that it determines in good faith, after consultation with such counsel, it is legally required to be disclosed, provided that the Disclosure Party exercise commercially reasonable efforts to preserve the confidentiality of the Evaluation Material and the Other Confidential Information, including, without limitation, by cooperating with the Other Party to obtain an appropriate protective order or other reliable assurance that confidential treatment will be accorded the Evaluation Material and the Other Confidential Information.</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>If either party decides that it does not wish to proceed with a transaction, it will promptly inform the other party of that decision. </SPAN 26><SPAN 27>In that case, or any time upon the request of a party for any reason, Vector will promptly, at Vector’s option </SPAN 27><SPAN 28>(i) return to Captaris and/or </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>(ii) destroy all Evaluation Material (and all tangible copies thereof) furnished to it or its Representatives by or on behalf of the other party pursuant hereto, and in either case no copies thereof shall be retained except that, any of the foregoing notwithstanding, that portion of the Evaluation Material that may be found in analyses, compilations, studies, or other documents prepared by Vector’s Representatives, such Representatives’ agents, attorneys or employees, and oral or electronic Evaluation Material will be held by such Representatives and kept subject to the terms of this agreement or destroyed to the extent practicable and permitted by law. </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>Notwithstanding the return or destruction of the Evaluation Material, each party and its Representatives will continue to be bound by the obligations of confidentiality and other obligations hereunder. </SPAN 30><SPAN 31>Notwithstanding the foregoing, </SPAN 31><SPAN 32>(i) financial advisors to the parties may retain copies of the Evaluation Material and Other Confidential Information (including Evaluation Material and Other Confidential Information) stored on electronic, magnetic or similar media) in accordance with policies and procedures implemented in order to comply with legal and regulatory requirements and to demonstrate such financial advisor’s compliance with its obligations, and </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>(ii) Representatives that are accounting firms may retain copies of the Evaluation Material in accordance with policies and procedures implemented by such persons in order to comply with applicable law, regulation, professional standards or reasonable business practice, and furthermore our Representatives that are accounting firms may disclose Evaluation Material to the extent required by law, rule, regulation or applicable professional standards of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants, Public Company Accounting Oversight Board or state boards of accountancy or obligations thereunder.</SPAN 33>
<SPAN 34>Vector understands and acknowledges that, except pursuant to a final definitive agreement regarding any transactions contemplated hereby, when, as and if executed, and subject to such limitations and restrictions as may be specified therein, </SPAN 34><SPAN 35>(i) neither Captaris nor any of’ its Representatives make any representation or warranty, express or implied, as to the accuracy or completeness of the Evaluation Material, </SPAN 35><SPAN 36>(ii) neither Captaris nor its Representatives shall have any liability to Vector or to any of its Representatives relating to or resulting from the use of the Evaluation Material or any errors therein or omissions therefrom, and </SPAN 36><SPAN 37>(iii) only those representations or warranties which are made in any such final definitive agreement will have any legal effect.</SPAN 37>
<SPAN 38>Captaris agrees that, for a period ending eight weeks after the date of this letter agreement, it will afford Vector and its Representatives, reasonable access to the information described in Exhibit A and the books, contracts, commitments and records of Captaris and its subsidiaries relevant thereto, unless and until Vector and Captaris have reached a non-binding consensus regarding basic deal terms, at which time access will broaden to include all other information concerning the business, properties and personnel (subject to restrictions imposed by applicable law) of Captaris and its Subsidiaries as Vector may reasonably request and that is in the possession or control of Captaris.</SPAN 38>
<SPAN 39>In consideration of the Evaluation Material being furnished by Captaris hereunder, Vector hereby agrees that, for a period of twelve months from the date hereof, it will not, and will not encourage or assist its affiliates to, solicit for employment </SPAN 39><SPAN 40>(a) any officers or other senior key employees of Captaris or any of its business units so long as they are employed by the Captaris or its business units, without obtaining the prior written consent of Captaris, and </SPAN 40><SPAN 41>(b) any of the other employees of Captaris or any of its business units with whom Vector has had contact or who Vector first became aware of during the period of its investigation of Captaris, so long as they are employed by the Captaris or its business units, without obtaining the prior written consent of Captaris. </SPAN 41><SPAN 42>Nothing in the foregoing clause </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>(b) shall preclude Vector from hiring any person who </SPAN 43><SPAN 44>(i) initiates discussions with Vector regarding such employment without any direct or indirect solicitation by Vector, </SPAN 44><SPAN 45>(ii) has ceased to be employed by Captaris prior to commencement of direct or indirect employment discussions between Vector and such person, or </SPAN 45><SPAN 46>(iii) responds to any general solicitation placed by Vector or any recruitment agency on Vector’s behalf.</SPAN 46>
<SPAN 47>Vector agrees that, for a period (the “Standstill Period”) ending on the earliest of </SPAN 47><SPAN 48>(i) six months from the date of this agreement and </SPAN 48><SPAN 49>(ii) the occurrence of a “Significant Event” (as defined below), unless it shall have been specifically invited in writing by Captaris, neither Vector nor any of its affiliates (as such term is defined under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”)) will in any manner, directly or indirectly, </SPAN 49><SPAN 50>(a) effect or publicly seek, offer or propose to effect, or cause or participate in or in any way assist any other person to effect or publicly seek, offer or propose to effect or participate in, </SPAN 50><SPAN 51>(i) any acquisition of 5% or more of the securities (or beneficial ownership thereof) or consolidated assets (including securities of subsidiaries) of Captaris; </SPAN 51><SPAN 52>(ii) any tender or exchange offer, merger or other business combination involving Captaris or any of its subsidiaries; </SPAN 52><SPAN 53>(iii) any recapitalization, restructuring, liquidation, dissolution or other extraordinary transaction with respect to Captaris or any of its subsidiaries; or </SPAN 53><SPAN 54>(iv) any “solicitation” of “proxies” (as such terms are used in the proxy rules of the Securities and Exchange Commission) or consents to vote any voting securities of Captaris; </SPAN 54><SPAN 55>(b) form, join or in any way participate in a “group” (as defined under the 1934 Act) the purpose of which is to effect a transaction described in </SPAN 55><SPAN 56>(a) above; </SPAN 56><SPAN 57>(c) otherwise act, alone or in concert with others, to publicly seek to control or influence the management, Board of Directors or policies of Captaris; or </SPAN 57><SPAN 58>(d) take any action which would reasonably be expected to force Captaris to make a public announcement regarding any of’ the types of matters set forth in </SPAN 58><SPAN 59>(a) above; provided, however, that, notwithstanding the foregoing, actions otherwise prohibited by clause </SPAN 59><SPAN 60>(a)(iv) above shall be permitted hereunder on the date thirty days prior to the last day on which shareholders may properly nominate directors for election at, and properly bring (but, for the avoidance of doubt, not by means of Rule 14a-8 under the Exchange Act) other business to be transacted at, Captaris’s 2008 annual meeting of shareholders if such date occurs earlier than the expiration of the Standstill Period as a result of </SPAN 60><SPAN 61>(x) the date of such meeting being advanced to be more than 30 days prior to the anniversary of Captaris’s 2007 annual meeting of shareholders and/or </SPAN 61><SPAN 62>(y) an amendment to Captaris’s Amended and Restated Bylaws. </SPAN 62><SPAN 63>For purposes of this agreement, </SPAN 63><SPAN 64>(i) ”Significant Event” shall mean </SPAN 64><SPAN 65>(A) the entry by Captaris into an agreement providing for, or the board of directors of Captaris otherwise recommending to the stockholders of Captaris, any merger, sale, stock issuance or other business combination transaction pursuant to which the outstanding shares of Captaris common stock would be converted into cash or securities of another person or 13D Group, or 20% or more of the then outstanding shares of Captaris common stock would be owned by persons other than the then current holders of shares of Captaris common stock, or which would result in all or a substantial portion of Captaris’s assets being sold to any person or 13D Group, or the outstanding shares of Captaris common stock immediately prior to any such transaction would constitute less than 80% of the outstanding shares of Captaris common stock immediately after such transaction, or </SPAN 65><SPAN 66>(B) an unsolicited bona fide tender offer or exchange offer is made by any person or 13D Group to acquire securities of Captaris which would (when added to shares already owned by such person or 13D Group) represent 20% or more of the then outstanding shares of Captaris common stock; </SPAN 66><SPAN 67>(ii) ”Voting Securities” shall mean shares of any class of Captaris capital stock which are then entitled to vote generally in the election of directors; provided, that for purposes of this definition any securities which at such time are convertible or exchangeable into or exercisable for shares of Captaris common stock shall be deemed to have been so converted, exchanged or exercised; and </SPAN 67><SPAN 68>(iii) ”13D Group” shall mean, with respect to Captaris Voting Securities, any group of persons formed for the purpose of acquiring, holding, voting or disposing of Captaris Voting Securities, which would require under Section 13(d) of the Exchange Act and the rules and regulations thereunder, the filing of a statement on Schedule 13D with the SEC as a “person” within the meaning of Section 13(d)(3) of the Exchange Act, if such group beneficially owned Captaris Voting Securities representing more than 5% of the total combined voting power of all Captaris Voting Securities then outstanding.</SPAN 68>
<SPAN 69>The parties understand and agree that no contract or agreement providing for any transaction between them shall be deemed to exist unless and until a final definitive agreement has been executed and delivered, and each party hereby waives, in advance, any claims (including, without limitation, breach of contract) in connection with any transaction involving the other party unless and until both parties shall have entered into a final definitive agreement. </SPAN 69><SPAN 70>Each party also agrees that unless and until a final definitive agreement regarding a transaction between the parties has been executed and delivered, neither party will be under any legal obligation of any kind whatsoever with respect to such a transaction by virtue of this letter agreement except for the matters specifically agreed to herein. </SPAN 70><SPAN 71>Each party further acknowledges and agrees that the other party reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to reject any and all proposals with regard to a transaction between the parties, and to terminate discussions and negotiations at any time. </SPAN 71><SPAN 72>Vector further understands that </SPAN 72><SPAN 73>(i) Captaris and its Representatives shall be free to conduct any process for any transaction involving Captaris, if and as they in their sole discretion shall determine (including, without limitation, negotiating with any other interested parties and entering into a definitive agreement without prior notice to Vector or any other person), </SPAN 73><SPAN 74>(ii) any procedures relating to such process or transaction may be changed at any time without notice to Vector or any other person, and </SPAN 74><SPAN 75>(iii) Vector shall not have any claims whatsoever against Captaris, its Representatives or any of their respective directors, officers, stockholders, owners, affiliates or agents arising out of or relating to any transaction involving Captaris (other than those as against the parties to a definitive agreement with Vector in accordance with the terms thereof) nor, unless a definitive agreement is entered into with Vector, against any third party with whom a transaction is entered into.</SPAN 75>
<SPAN 76>It is understood and agreed that no failure or delay by either party in exercising any right, power or privilege hereunder shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise thereof preclude any other or future exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right, power or privilege hereunder.</SPAN 76>
<SPAN 77>It is further understood and agreed that money damages would not be a sufficient remedy for any breach of this letter agreement by either party or any of its Representatives and that the parties shall be entitled to seek equitable relief, including injunction and specific performance, as a remedy for any such breach. </SPAN 77><SPAN 78>Such remedies shall not be deemed to be the exclusive remedies for a breach of this letter agreement but shall be in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity. </SPAN 78><SPAN 79>In the event of litigation relating to this letter agreement, if a court of competent jurisdiction determines in a final, non-appealable order that a party has breached this letter agreement, then such party shall be liable and pay to the non-breaching party the reasonable legal fees incurred by such non-breaching party in connection with such litigation, including any appeal therefrom. </SPAN 79><SPAN 80>This letter agreement is for the benefit of the parties and their respective directors, officers, stockholders, owners, affiliates, and agents, and shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York.</SPAN 80>
<SPAN 81>This letter agreement will terminate on the second anniversary of the date of this agreement.</SPAN 81>
<SPAN 82>Please confirm your agreement with the foregoing by signing and returning one copy of this letter to the undersigned, whereupon this letter agreement shall become a binding agreement between Vector and Captaris.</SPAN 82>
<SPAN 83>Very truly yours,</SPAN 83>
<SPAN 84>Captaris, Inc.</SPAN 84>
<SPAN 85>By: /s/ David P. Anastasi</SPAN 85>
<SPAN 86>Its: President & CEO</SPAN 86>
<SPAN 87>Accepted and agreed as of the date first written above:</SPAN 87>
<SPAN 88>Vector Capital Corporation</SPAN 88>
<SPAN 89>By: /s/ Amish Mehta</SPAN 89>
<SPAN 90>Its: Partner</SPAN 90>

guidance.when: Assessing whether return or destruction is required when the agreement or protected evaluation ends.
guidance.inspection: Identify both the required act and its trigger. Termination or expiration qualifies, as does an expressly stated conclusion, rejection, or abandonment of the evaluation or business possibility. A request-only duty or a party's mere decision not to proceed does not qualify without language making an end event itself the trigger.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative return-or-destruction duty and the language establishing its end-event trigger. Include every independent termination-triggered return or deletion obligation relied upon.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exception to a return or destruction obligation.
guidance.inspection: Check whether the exception expressly permits continued possession of backups, archival material, a legal copy, or another defined subset after the return/destruction event. Conditions on access, purpose, or continuing confidentiality do not negate the permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention exception and, when separated, the governing return/destruction clause showing the temporal context.

guidance.when: The agreement requires return or destruction of confidential information and copies without stating a retention exception.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether the duty is exhaustive as to the covered material and copies. A complete return/destruction command that leaves no authorized retained subset negates permission to possess some material afterward.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the exhaustive operative duty and verify across the complete agreement that no backup, archival, legal-copy, or other retention exception qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses ownership, licenses, or rights in confidential information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Look for language that no license or right is granted, conveyed, conferred, or implied. A limited authorization to review or use information for the stated transaction does not by itself contradict the broader no-grant proposition.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the express no-grant clause; include an ownership clause only when it helps establish the object of the denied rights.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts disclosure of negotiations, discussions, a contemplated transaction, the agreement itself, or the existence of dealings.
guidance.inspection: A prohibition on revealing that negotiations or discussions exist establishes the hypothesis. A prohibition on public announcements concerning the agreement or transaction also qualifies; definition text alone must be paired with an operative nondisclosure duty.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative prohibition and the protected fact, retaining any governing introduction needed to connect a listed fact to the prohibition.

guidance.when: Confidential-information coverage is conditioned on marking, designation, or identification by the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the identification condition grammatically governs every covered disclosure mode. A single terminal condition may govern an enumeration of oral, written, and electronic modes; different procedures may also govern different modes. Do not treat nature- or circumstances-based coverage as identification.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete definition or all clauses needed to show that every disclosure mode is subject to identification by the disclosing party.

guidance.when: The definition covers information either expressly designated confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential from its nature or disclosure circumstances.
guidance.inspection: The contextual alternative independently covers undesignated information, so express identification by the disclosing party is not required for all confidential information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete alternative definition showing both designation and circumstance- or nature-based coverage.

guidance.when: Assessing whether the receiving party may make a copy in some circumstance.
guidance.inspection: Require an affirmative operational copying route, such as copies necessary for authorized use or acknowledged automatic backups. A prohibition phrased as applying without prior consent or approval is not by itself an affirmative permission to copy.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite language affirmatively authorizing, requiring, or acknowledging copy creation and its governing condition; disclosure or access permission is insufficient.

guidance.when: The agreement prohibits copying confidential information and contains no affirmative operational copying route.
guidance.inspection: A direct copy ban, including a ban stated as applying without prior consent or approval, negates the benchmark permission hypothesis when the complete agreement does not otherwise authorize necessary copies, backups, or another copying circumstance. Do not convert the consent qualifier itself into affirmative permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the copy prohibition and verify across the agreement that no affirmative operational-copy or backup route qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure to representatives or other persons.
guidance.inspection: Resolve who falls within the permitted class. Consultants, agents, counsel, accountants, professional advisers, affiliates, and similar non-employees establish sharing with some third parties; an employee-only exception does not.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the permission and the definition or enumeration proving that at least one permitted recipient is a third party, plus any need-to-know or confidentiality condition governing the permission.

guidance.when: The agreement states an authorized transaction, project, evaluation, business relationship, or other defined purpose for confidential information.
guidance.inspection: A command to use confidential information only for that purpose, or not for any other purpose, directly imposes the limited-use obligation. The existence of the authorized purpose is not a contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use restriction and enough purpose language to identify the authorized scope.

guidance.when: Relevant candidate text is a numbered item, exception, continuation, anaphoric clause, or otherwise incomplete fragment.
guidance.inspection: Read the governing introduction and adjacent items to determine the item's legal function, trigger, subject, and exceptions. Keep independent operative clauses separately; do not treat a neighboring item as evidence merely because it shares the list.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every span necessary to make the relied-on proposition complete, while excluding sibling items that do not establish that proposition.

guidance.when: The confidential-information definition enumerates subject matter or data categories.
guidance.inspection: Find an expressly covered non-technical category, such as business, financial, marketing, personnel, customer, contact, or transaction information. Generic references to all information, documents, analyses, form, or derivatives do not alone prove non-technical coverage.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the definition and at least one explicit non-technical category; include continuation text when the category list crosses fragments.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exclusion, reservation, or acknowledgment concerning independent development.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the receiving party may develop information independently without using or accessing the protected information. Prior approval to disclose, lawful receipt, or another unrelated exception does not establish independent development.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the independent-development clause with its governing exclusion or reservation language when needed to make its legal function complete.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses information obtained from an external source or made available non-confidentially.
guidance.inspection: Look for lawful receipt from a source other than the disclosing party that is not bound by confidentiality, or for the disclosing party's later non-confidential release making the information externally available. Independent development and consent to the receiver's own disclosure are different matters.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the external-source or non-confidential-release clause and its governing exclusion introduction, including any condition concerning the source's authority or confidentiality duties.

guidance.when: The definition or coverage clause addresses communication form.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether oral or verbal communication is expressly within confidential information, including language covering information irrespective of communication form or information disclosed in writing and also orally. Do not infer oral coverage merely from derivative notes or documents.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the language linking oral, verbal, or form-independent communication to confidential-information coverage, with any necessary definition continuation.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts recruiting, hiring, employment contact, or solicitation involving personnel of the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Find a prohibition on soliciting, employing, hiring, or initiating employment contact with officers, employees, or other personnel. Proxy solicitation, transaction standstill language, and general contact restrictions are not personnel nonsolicitation unless tied to employment or hiring.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative employment-related prohibition and the covered personnel class; include duration, targeting limits, or recruiting exceptions when they qualify the prohibition.

guidance.when: The agreement states that duties continue beyond an end event or remain effective for a post-event period.
guidance.inspection: Verify that confidentiality, non-use, or another agreement obligation continues after termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or an equivalent end of the protected relationship. Continuation merely after return or destruction does not establish survival of agreement termination.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the continuing obligation and the termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or equivalent end event to which continuation is linked.
